title: Collapse duplicate equality/hashCode/toString assertions inside delta_value_test.dart

evidence.quote:
test('equality: not equal to different type', () {
      expect(const DateDelta(5) == const PaceDelta(5), isFalse);

test('equality: DateDelta != PaceDelta with same numeric value', () {
      expect(const DateDelta(5) == const PaceDelta(5), isFalse);

why: Within this single 290-line file, several test() blocks are byte-for-byte identical in body under different names — e.g. lines 27-29 and 31-33 both assert `DateDelta(5) == PaceDelta(5)` is false; lines 39-41 and 47-49 both assert DateDelta(5).hashCode equality the same way; lines 51-53 and 55-57 both assert DateDelta(7).toString() contains '7'. Harmless (both copies pass and are correct) but purely additive noise: roughly 6 of the file's ~50 tests contribute zero incremental coverage over their twin, inflating the file for a future reader trying to find what's actually pinned.
recommendation: Delete one test from each identified duplicate pair, keeping the more descriptively-named one.
acceptance_criteria: No two test() bodies in the file are textually identical (grep/diff check).

corrections: 'sites: 1' undercounts — the file actually has ~3 duplicate-body test pairs (lines 27-33, 39-49 functionally, 51-57), not 1. Still correctly filed as ONE finding per the one-finding-per-root-cause rule; just the count is off.

The hashCode example (lines 39-41 vs 47-49) is functionally but not textually identical (equals() wrapper differs), contradicting the finding's 'byte-for-byte identical' framing for that specific pair; the other two cited pairs (27-33, 51-57) ARE byte-for-byte identical as claimed, and the ~6-of-50 aggregate count is accurate.
